transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is this tension. My shoulders and neck... they just stay clenched all day long. It's like I'm bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the evening, my jaw aches so badly from clenching it that I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar anymore. It's just constant.
How long have you been experiencing this constant muscle tension and jaw clenching—has it been going on for several months or longer, or did it start more recently after a particular event?

It's been longer than just a few months. I'd say... it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It all started right after a specific event, actually—right after I was fired from the preschool.
Besides the physical tension, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things in your life—like finances, family, health, or work—even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Yes, I do. It's pretty much constant, honestly. My mind just keeps circling from one thing to the next. 

I'll worry about whether I'll ever get hired again, and then that turns into wondering if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents in the community. Then I start stressing about my finances and whether my retirement is just slipping away from me at this age. It even gets down to these little details—like, I'll worry that a small mistake I made during a story-time activity means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. It just doesn't turn off.
Along with the worry and muscle tension, have you noticed other changes like feeling unusually irritable, tired, or having trouble sleeping most days?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely been affected. Most nights I just... I lie in bed for hours. I end up replaying interview answers in my head, or thinking about bills, or stressing over licensing forms. It's hard to shut it off. 

And even when I do finally manage to fall asleep, it doesn't last. I almost always wake up around four in the morning. I wake up already tense, just calculating everything that could possibly go wrong that day. So because of that, yeah, I am pretty tired most of the time.
